newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says free trade rules prevail against pharmaceutical patent holders.
newsitem.headline: Court says free trade rules prevail against pharmaceutical patent holders.

text.p: The European Court of Justice prohibited on Thursday member state rules which allow pharmaceutical patent holders to oppose parallel imports of their products from other member states.

Ruling in two cases from Britain between industry giants Merck & Co and the Beecham Group plc against the smaller Primecrown Ltd and Europharm Ltd, the court recalled its reasoning in the 1981 "Merck v Stephar" case.

The court held in "Merck" that if the holder of a patent decided to sell its product in a member state which did not provide patent protection, "he must then accept the consequences of his choice as regards free movement of the product within the common market...."

The court said the aim of the EU Treaty to create a common market, with particular reference to articles 30 and 36, would be undermined if an inventor could invoke a patent held in one member state to prevent the import of a product freely marketed by the inventor in another member state.
The court rejected arguments from Merck and Beecham that the reasoning in "Merck" has changed because most pharmaceutical products now must be patented in all member states.

"The arguments put forward in the present cases have not shown that the court was wrong in its assessment of the balance between the principle of free movement of goods in the Community and the principle of protection of patentees' rights...," the court said.

The court also ruled that the transitional period for Spain and Portugal, as applied to pharmaceutical products under their accession treaties to the EU, expired on 6 October 1995 and 31 December 1994, respectively.

on the interpretation of article 47 and article 209 of the Act concerning the Conditions of Accession of the Kingdom of Spain and the Portuguese Republic and the Adjustments to the Treaties (OJ 1985 L 302, p. 23), and of articles 30 and 36 of the EC Treaty
THE COURT hereby rules

1. The transitional periods provided for in articles 47 and 209 of the Act concerning the Conditions of Accession of the Kingdom of Spain and the Portuguese Republic and the Adjustments to the Treaties expired on 6 October 1995 in the case of the Kingdom of Spain and on 31 December 1994 in the case of the Portuguese Republic.

2. Articles 30 and 36 of the EC Treaty preclude applicaiton of national legislation which grants the holder of a patent for a pharmaceutical product the right to oppose importation by a third party of that product from another member state in circumstances where the holder first put the product on the market in that state after its accession to the European Community but before the product could be protected by a patent in that state, unless the holder of the patent can prove that he is under a genuine, existing legal obligation to market the product in that member state.
